batch_strategy: Select 32 distinct experiments, with their supplied premeasurement predictions fixed unchanged as one batch. Emphasize remaining solvent-ratio gaps, matched loading contrasts, and scaffold-specific completion behavior. Use paired measurements where they distinguish competing response shapes; avoid selecting multiple IDs for the same encoded experiment.

choices.reason: Measure m75 at 10/1 and 109.5 mg between measured 54.75 and 164.25 mg anchors. Their V1 values differ by 4.95 mL while V2 differs by only 0.38 mL (ce3b9d9cbe1699c7eef9; dea5f0228035f44dd102). This middle point tests onset-response curvature independently of completion.

The m82 5/1, 51.45 mg point opens an unmeasured solvent segment below its measured 10/1 and 20/1 branches (6b8e53d2d8c8a90a7216; 61090cfdcf019e0891a3). Paired with the selected higher load, it tests whether the model's nearly invariant loading forecasts miss an onset response in this beta-ketoester.

This m82 5/1, 154.35 mg experiment completes the selected loading contrast. Existing higher-load 10/1 and 20/1 measurements show substantial completion growth (5b7151c95c4e964a121b; b6bf451b4911ee22d4a4); the new pair determines how early that response develops and whether loading changes the endpoints differently.

The m25 5/1, 95.4 mg point fills a solvent gap before measured 10/1, 20/1 and 50/1 retention growth (d21f08a7e8eaa163ecfc; 327064e6ca2c38d79d76; 3fc05dc2025715e68174). It provides a tert-butyl beta-ketoester comparison to the selected m82 pair without assuming their response knees coincide.

Measure m189 at 5/1 with the same loading as its measured 2/1 and 20/1 anchors (f1dafc187f7b1ec15297; fd9cda2d3ab32ea2a360). The forecast is 6.00/23.16 mL. Together with the selected 10/1 point, this locates completion curvature in a biphenyl aldehyde near the nonmonotonic ketone behavior measured for m68.

The m174 50/1, 54.85 mg point extends a lower-load curve whose 20/1 behavior differs substantially from higher loading (91161a9006beb2042fa7; 591b1bb527d42e831f12). Comparing it with measured 50/1 higher-load anchors tests whether that loading dependence persists or diminishes.

This m174 100/1, 54.85 mg point joins the selected 50/1 experiment and measured 100/1 higher loads (2424b103c34d3d2b6a9a; 36b45fbdbace5950c108). It distinguishes solvent-dependent amplification from a nearly constant loading response in benzyl benzoate.

The m166 20/1, 50 mg measurement extends measured 100 and 150 mg completion anchors of 28.43 and 31.34 mL (80de1b57c56257d2ecae; 4c2ad10692512e8f23b8). It tests whether completion varies smoothly with loading while onset remains near the early-elution branch, and matches the selected m167 conditions.

Measure m167 at 20/1 and 50 mg alongside m166 under identical recorded conditions. The forecast of 6.79/21.01 mL tests the intervening solvent response between measured 10/1 and 50/1 higher-load anchors (25dd969086d07da70d74; fa6fd34875fdc7acf6c1), while the pair probes how aromatic extension changes completion.

The m168 50/1, 40 mg point uses 300 uL DCM and supplies the lower end of a matched loading panel around the measured 80 mg experiment, 5ba8cead5a790ba93029. Its broad single-model quantile spans support checking this endpoint response, but do not establish epistemic uncertainty.

This m168 50/1, 120 mg point completes the selected panel at constant loading-solvent identity and volume. Predictions for 40 and 120 mg are nearly identical, whereas the measured 80 mg completion is 28.17 mL (5ba8cead5a790ba93029). The panel tests whether the remaining loading response is flat, curved, or endpoint-specific.

Measure m38 at 5/1 and 100 mg between measured 50 and 150 mg anchors (bfcb567664468f0d6902; 5b1b0390c90ceb580c5e). Increasing load moved onset earlier but completion later across those anchors. The middle label tests whether both trends interpolate smoothly and helps repair completion without imposing an onset shift.

The m40 2/1, 168 mg point extends the recently measured 56 mg anchor, where onset was underpredicted by 2.60 mL (551ec1f8caaa42f2e478). This tests whether that onset discrepancy is confined to lower loading or transfers across the loading range of a fused aromatic ketone.

The m192 5/1, 169.8 mg experiment adds a solvent anchor matched to measured 10/1 and 50/1 rows (1125dd6a2736e219401f; 253f25857da206693a36). Recent 2/1 feedback showed a completion-specific underprediction at higher loading (d170227948f0f7b43616), motivating a local curve check for this chloro/bromo aldehyde.

Measure m130 in pure EA at 50 mg. The model forecasts an unusually early onset of 2.64 mL with completion at 14.29 mL. Paired with the selected 1/1 experiment, this tests whether the large predicted onset change is real or a strong-eluent modeling artifact; existing 5/1 and 20/1 anchors provide context (99fb49a26d4f0f1440df; b2ac848cc42390b01b9f).

This m130 1/1, 50 mg experiment is predicted at 8.54/14.37 mL, compared with 2.64/14.29 mL for the selected pure-EA row. The matched pair distinguishes an onset-specific solvent extremum from bias while holding all other supplied conditions fixed.

The m53 1/1, 88.8 mg point tests a predicted endpoint reversal relative to the selected pure-EA condition: onset increases while completion decreases. Measured 10/1 and 20/1 higher-load anchors show subsequent retention growth (87d4aa727f2254c554ac; c5b88ffca991e883ab64), but do not determine this strong-eluent segment.

Measure m53 in pure EA at 88.8 mg alongside its selected 1/1 counterpart. This supplies an unmeasured baseline for an acyclic conjugated aldehyde and tests whether the predicted completion rebound occurs outside aromatic scaffolds, where such behavior cannot safely be transferred from structural analogy.

The m34 pure-EA, 114.3 mg point establishes the baseline for the selected 1/1 experiment. Its forecast of 4.48/10.86 mL contrasts with 4.78/16.26 mL at 1/1; measured 5/1 anchors establish nearby completion around 15.5–16.5 mL (059b09a46d0835771fd6; f5d873a623aaeeb1e41e).

Measure m12 in pure EA at 99.6 mg. With the selected 1/1 row and measured 5/1 anchor dbe79bb4ca4ae4967721, it tests the predicted strong-eluent onset and completion rebounds in a donor-free hydrocarbon. Measured m10 and m7 curves show that low-polarity scaffolds need separate solvent-response anchors.

This m12 1/1, 99.6 mg point completes the matched strong-eluent pair. Forecasts place onset earlier than in pure EA while completion changes only modestly. Measuring both determines whether that curvature is supported and avoids extrapolating the measured 5/1 behavior into an uncovered solvent segment.

The m21 1/1, 55.2 mg point anchors an unmeasured strong-eluent segment for a phenoxyethyl acrylate. Existing 10/1 and 50/1 measurements at this load differ substantially (487606cee9b08ded91f3; b4351e5f05f6d477a6c0); the selected 1/1 and 2/1 pair tests whether the forecast early plateau is supported.

Measure m21 at 2/1 and 55.2 mg, matched to the selected 1/1 row. Predictions change little and slightly decrease both endpoints as eluent weakens. This pair discriminates a local plateau or reversal from model bias and informs response transfer among ether-containing acrylates.

The m144 20/1, 148.35 mg point fills the interval between measured 10/1 and 50/1 conditions (101e73ea321226570290; 1c312750e15ff66c6243). It locates the weak-eluent response knee for an ortho-methyl aryl nitrile instead of borrowing the curves of the measured ortho-fluoro and ortho-bromo nitriles.

This m144 5/1, 148.35 mg point complements the selected 20/1 anchor and measured 1/1 and 10/1 rows (97fda03b3c38e5bc5abd; 101e73ea321226570290). Its onset forecast of 6.75 mL exceeds the measured 10/1 onset of 5.80 mL, motivating a direct test of an interior reversal versus forecast bias.

Measure m100 at 20/1 and 49.75 mg between matched-load 5/1 and 50/1 observations (20ef1039f09d571c5a09; c5a12771920c4410d921). This tests whether completion remains on a plateau before rising at weak eluent in a tert-butyl-substituted benzoate, providing a useful boundary for transfer from other ester curves.

The m56 100/1, 49.8 mg point extends the lower-load isobutyl benzoate series and contrasts with measured 149.4 mg at 100/1 (e7c4d856d4d9a8d5ddbf). The measured lower-load 40/1 anchor ac76ec24edfe8aec7fb2 helps distinguish solvent curvature from loading effects on completion.

Measure m206 in pure EA at 100 mg, matched to measured 1/1 and 2/1 anchors (53ceb391785085223695; 13bfaf03c35b4cff3bd5). This establishes how onset approaches its early-elution baseline while completion contracts in a strongly retained aromatic alcohol, without transferring the pure-EA behavior of phenols.

The m216 10/1, 163.95 mg point extends a basic heteroaromatic loading curve whose measured 54.65 and 109.3 mg onsets differ substantially while completion is nearly unchanged (e47aebe2660b9e1528de; 9cd02352c2ed7a3e2321). It tests saturation or reversal beyond the middle load, a relationship not covered by the recent low-polarity controls.

Measure m34 at 1/1 and 114.3 mg alongside the selected pure-EA condition. Broad single-predictor quantile spans and the unmeasured strong-eluent segment motivate this pair. It tests whether completion already approaches the measured 5/1 range while onset remains low.

The m32 1/1, 100.4 mg point adds a strong-eluent anchor for a related para-substituted acetophenone. At this load, measured 10/1 and 20/1 completions differ nonmonotonically (e23428098aa1cdad35be; ee5c9d29ed57c3312389). It complements m34 while retaining its distinct recorded DCM loading context, so the comparison is not treated as an isolated substituent effect.

This m189 10/1 experiment completes the selected 5/1–10/1 interior panel between measured 2/1 and 20/1 anchors. It tests the forecast completion maximum and onset hump. The measured m68 5/1-to-10/1 completion decrease (c4b06a6e718225cb9cf8; f1e08c239f1c0950ad36) supplies a relevant analogy, not evidence that m189 must follow it.

hypotheses.content: Changing the recorded sample load at otherwise matched catalog conditions can affect onset and completion differently; the magnitude and even direction depend on scaffold and solvent ratio. A universal loading offset is inadequate.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The latest m75 and m38 labels reinforce endpoint-specific loading responses, while m174 shows that response direction cannot be transferred universally. Matched panels and interior loading points can teach these interactions without coupling V1 and V2 corrections.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the remaining m82, m168, m174 and m216 loading extensions follow smooth curves, saturate, or change direction, and which endpoint carries the response?

hypotheses.content: Completion corrections must be localized to scaffold-condition neighborhoods. Some carbonyl systems show substantial completion underprediction with a relatively accurate onset, but carbonyl functionality alone does not justify a shared positive V2 correction.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The supplied feedback contains both completion underprediction and overprediction, plus accurately predicted carbonyl examples. Local solvent and loading panels can teach the boundary of each response instead of spreading an inappropriate correction across the chemical family.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m189 reproduce a local completion maximum resembling m68, and do matched m166/m167 measurements reveal a transferable aromatic-extension effect or distinct completion curves?

hypotheses.content: Solvent-response curvature is scaffold- and endpoint-specific. Some measured curves are nonmonotonic, so local anchors should determine whether a predicted plateau or extremum reflects the recorded response or model bias.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The remaining pool contains several uncovered strong-eluent segments and interior ratio gaps. Matched pairs across nitrile, aldehyde, ketone, hydrocarbon and acrylate contexts can separate endpoint response shapes and reduce inappropriate transfer of a common solvent curve.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Are the predicted strong-eluent onset or completion reversals in m130, m53, m12 and m21 supported, and where do the m144 and ester response knees lie?

feedback_interpretation: The latest outcomes support a more selective use of loading experiments. For m75, the measured 54.75-to-164.25 mg contrast changes V1 from 12.68 to 7.73 mL while V2 remains near 19 mL. For m38, higher loading moves onset earlier and completion later. These strengthen endpoint-specific loading learning. Completion underpredictions for m38, m192 and m14 remain useful failure evidence, but m176 had a completion overprediction, and the m168 pure-EA and m94 10/1 labels were close to their acquisition forecasts. Thus a broad carbonyl completion correction is less defensible than local scaffold-condition repair. Several recent low-polarity controls also had modest errors, reducing the value of another broad collection of similar loading controls. Historical acquisition errors are not current-model residuals. I also corrected inherited annotations using the supplied conditions and SMILES: PE/EA 0/1 is pure EA, m199 is a sulfoxide, and m192 is a chloro/bromo aldehyde. Inconsistent labels at identical encoded conditions elsewhere in the trajectory caution against interpreting every anomaly as a deterministic chemical effect.
batch_rationale: The batch targets unmeasured encoded conditions rather than duplicate candidate IDs for already sampled experiments. Its main experiments are matched strong-eluent pairs, interior solvent panels, and loading extensions supported by measured endpoint differences. The m82 and m25 choices locate beta-ketoester response development; m166/m167 and m189 test how completion relationships transfer within aromatic carbonyl neighborhoods; m168, m174 and m216 test different loading-response regimes. The m130, m53, m12, m21 and m34 pairs directly discriminate predicted solvent-response shapes, while m144, m100, m56 and m206 fill gaps next to measured anchors. All selected molecules already occur in L_t, so exploration here concerns uncovered structure-condition relationships. Quantile spans and CW distances are secondary evidence, not calibrated epistemic uncertainty. Loading-amount contrasts also change V/ul at fixed density and therefore teach the joint recorded loading response; they do not independently identify mass and sample-volume effects. The combination should improve Row-distribution generalization by refining endpoint-specific responses across recurring chemical families while limiting unsupported transfer of global loading or completion corrections.
